newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares rise sharply in thin trading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares rise sharply in thin trading.

text.p: Israeli shares closed sharply higher on Tuesday in what traders said was a technical rebound following last week's sharp decline.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of top 100 shares rose 2.82 percent, or 6.96 points, to 253.77 on a low all-share turnover of 92 million shekels against 93 million shekels on Monday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 2.93 percent higher at 263.12.

"The market lost almost 10 percent last week and now it's time for a correction. The rise of dollar against the shekel today is also seen as a positive development for Israeli exporters," said a trader at Tachlit Securities.
The representative rate for the dollar was fixed on Tuesday at 3.3630 shekels against 3.3530 on Monday after the U.S. currency rallied to a 34-month high against the mark.
"Investors panicked last week and the market fell too fast. The decline of the Maof below 260 was not justified and the market recovered today," said a trader at Bank Leumi.
"It is very difficult to say where the market is going. This may be the beginning of a new positive wave," the Tachlit trader said.
Traders noted that the low volume indicated that investors are still undecided about the market's direction.

Elbit Systems, surged 4.75 percent to 2,704 agorot. The company net profit fell in the fourth quarter of 1996 to $6.4 million from $7.3 million a year earlier. The company declared a dividend of $0.05 a share for the fourth quarter payable May 14.

The most active shares were Bank Leumi, which gained 2.75 percent to 544 agorot on turnover of 4.4 million shekels; Koor Industries, which rose 2.75 percent to 32,084 agorot on volume of 4.2 million shekels; and Israel Chemicals which surged 6.0 percent to 386 agorot on turnover of 3.8 million shekels.
